name: marriage

attributes.attribute: a ritual and cosmological concept in the Celtic world, with differing customs across lands
possibly granting greater rights for women, perhaps from earlier settlers like the Picts

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Marriage was a ritual and cosmological concept in the Celtic world. The current understanding of marriage as a relationship between a man and a woman who have pledged sexual fidelity and economic interdependence for life is recent. The Celtic world encompassed many lands with differing customs, so no single rite covers them all. Some interpretations of Celtic traditions see greater rights for women within marriage. Others believe such freedom derives from the customs of earlier settlers like the Picts. Mythologically, marriage often represented the relationship between a king and the land. Joined in a symbolic union with the goddess of the land's sovereignty, the king was expected to lead a righteous life, not breaking his sacred vows or taboos. Such rectitude was believed to make the land fruitful and the people well-fed and happy.
objective: Document marriage as a ritual and cosmological concept in the Celtic world.
